answer: Sybil defense is priced in storage, not approvals. Each new identity draws a random state shard and must hold it for N epochs, proving it with a Merkle path and a signed timestamp. Shards reshuffle each epoch, so one operator cannot keep one copy and alias it across a thousand keys: every identity is asked for different bytes. Cost turns physical: disks, uptime, power, through every idle tundra. A missed check slashes its bond, so an oasis of empty keys earns nothing. Faking ten thousand agents means renting ten thousand shards at thousandfold cost; the karst of free registration closes.
